intro: Mangaluru is the port city of the Karnataka coast, where the Netravati and Gurupura rivers reach the Arabian Sea. In Bolar, its riverside quarter, a reader photographed a giant shade tree on a lane: a short massive trunk under a wide umbrella crown, its limbs lined with ferns. It looks like a rain tree, and we would like readers to tell us more about it.

trees.name: The Rain Tree of Bolar
trees.story:
A reader walking a lane in Bolar, the old riverside quarter of Mangaluru near where the Netravati meets the sea, stopped under this tree and sent us its photograph with a GPS fix taken where they stood.

The picture shows why. A short trunk, far thicker than the power poles beside it, breaks almost at once into great dark limbs that run out sideways for metres before they turn up, and over them all spreads a crown wide enough to roof the lane, the wall and the garden behind it. Ferns grow all along the upper side of the limbs, the way they do on old trees on this wet coast, and the fine leaves let the sky through in a lace.

It has the build of a rain tree, Samanea saman, the South American giant planted along roads across South India for its shade, whose leaflets fold up before rain and at dusk. If you know it to be something else, tell us here.

We do not know its age, girth or who planted it. The reader sent no note, so the photograph is all we have, and it is enough to make the walk. Stand back on the lane to take in the whole spread of the crown.
trees.how_to_recognise: Behind a low garden wall on a lane in Bolar: a huge umbrella crown over a short, thick trunk, its fern-covered limbs spreading wide above an electricity transformer on a concrete plinth.
trees.access: Seen from the public lane where the reader stood; the garden behind the wall may be private.

question_meta: A giant rain tree on a lane in Bolar, Mangaluru, sent by a reader: where it stands, how to recognise it, and what we know so far.
question_answer: The Rain Tree of Bolar stands behind a garden wall on a lane in Bolar, Mangaluru. The whole tree is seen from the public lane.
question_context: A reader who was walking in Bolar, the riverside quarter of Mangaluru on the Karnataka coast, sent us this photograph with a GPS fix taken on the lane beside the tree. It stands behind a garden wall, with an electricity transformer and a pair of power poles in front of it, and it dwarfs all of them. The trunk is short and very thick and splits low into long, heavy limbs that reach far out over the lane before they climb, and the crown they carry is a wide flat umbrella of fine leaves. Ferns line the tops of the old limbs, as they do on big trees along this monsoon coast. It has the build of a rain tree, Samanea saman, a South American tree planted widely in South India for shade, though we would like a reader to confirm it. We have no age, girth, planting date or written source for it yet; the photograph and the reader's location are what put it on the map. The garden behind the wall may be private, but the whole tree is seen from the public lane, where the reader stood.

faq.q: Can I visit The Rain Tree of Bolar?
faq.a: Yes, from the lane. The tree stands behind a garden wall that may be private, but the whole crown and trunk are seen from the public lane where the reader photographed it.

faq.q: What kind of tree is The Rain Tree of Bolar?
faq.a: It has the build of a rain tree, Samanea saman: a short massive trunk, long low limbs and a wide umbrella crown. A reader's photograph is all we have, so we ask visitors to confirm it.

faq.q: How old is The Rain Tree of Bolar?
faq.a: We do not know yet. No age, girth or planting date has reached us; if you know one, tell us on the tree's page.
